findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the OIDC trust-policy (assume-role) condition for the new Bedrock CI role: constrain `token.actions.githubusercontent.com:aud` to `sts.amazonaws.com` AND `:sub` to this repo (and ideally the specific workflow/ref), matching the existing `rebar-terraform-plan` role's `repo:navapbc/rebar:*` scoping in iam.tf, so only the external-integration workflow can assume it.
evidence: Plan reuses 'S7's POLICY (reuse the policy shape, not the delivery path)' — the permission policy, not the trust policy; the trust/assume-role condition is unspecified.

Repo precedent shows the trust-scope discipline is expected: the existing OIDC role in infra/terraform/iam.tf:151-163 scopes `token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub` to `repo:navapbc/rebar:*` and the `aud` to `sts.amazonaws.com`, with a comment noting it can be narrowed to a specific ref.

S7 (rebar:9249) delivers only the least-privilege permission policy (iam_s7.tf) attached to an EC2 instance role reached via IMDS — it carries NO GitHub-OIDC trust policy, so 'model on S7's POLICY' gives the plan no trust-scoping template to inherit.
findings.finding: The plan mandates OIDC role assumption for the Bedrock arm but does not pin the trust-policy `sub` (subject) condition that scopes WHICH GitHub Actions principal may assume the dedicated Bedrock role. It specifies 'a dedicated, scoped Bedrock role modelled on S7's POLICY (reuse the policy shape, not the delivery path)' — i.e. it scopes the PERMISSION policy (which is least-privilege), but the trust/assume-role side is left as just 'OIDC federation ... plus aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials'. An OIDC-assumable role whose assume-role policy does not constrain `token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub` is assumable from arbitrary GitHub Actions workflows, not only this repo's external-integration workflow.
findings.location: Approach section, 'OIDC federation — permissions: id-token: write plus aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials assuming a dedicated, scoped Bedrock role modelled on S7's POLICY'; AC 'The Bedrock arm obtains credentials by a NAMED mechanism'
scenarios: An unrelated or forked GitHub repo/workflow presenting a valid GitHub OIDC token with aud=sts.amazonaws.com assumes the Bedrock role and issues live Bedrock InvokeModel calls, incurring spend and abusing the credentials.
The plan's own AC 'pins that it does not silently fall back to ANTHROPIC_API_KEY' passes while the trust boundary is still wide open.
findings.suggested_fix: In the Approach and the Bedrock-credential AC, require the new role's assume-role policy to federate `aws_iam_openid_connect_provider.github` with a `StringEquals` on `...:aud = sts.amazonaws.com` and a `StringLike`/`StringEquals` on `...:sub` pinned to `repo:navapbc/rebar:*` (or narrower, e.g. `repo:navapbc/rebar:ref:refs/heads/main` / the workflow that runs the external suite) — following the iam.tf:151-163 precedent — and add a CI/test assertion that the trust policy is so scoped.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the OIDC role's TRUST policy, not just its permission policy: pin the AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity condition to the specific repo + ref/workflow (`token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub` and `:aud`) so only this repo's external-integration workflow can assume the scoped Bedrock role, and add a CI/test assertion (or an explicit AC) that the trust condition is scoped rather than trusting the GitHub OIDC provider unconditionally.
evidence: Plan quote: 'a dedicated, scoped Bedrock role modelled on S7's POLICY (reuse the policy shape, not the delivery path)' — scopes the permission policy, silent on the trust policy
infra/terraform/iam.tf:16-28 — S7's role trusts a Service principal (ec2.amazonaws.com), so 'reuse S7's policy shape' provides no trust-policy model for a GitHub web-identity role
Trust boundary: GitHub OIDC provider (token.actions.githubusercontent.com) is an external IdP federated into the AWS account; the role is the boundary-crossing credential the plan itself creates
STRIDE-Spoofing / least-privilege: an unscoped web-identity trust condition lets a lower-trust actor (another repo/branch) assume the Bedrock role
findings.finding: The plan creates a new AWS IAM role assumable via GitHub OIDC federation but specifies only its PERMISSION policy ('modelled on S7's POLICY'), never its TRUST policy — the AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity condition scoping which GitHub repo/ref/workflow may assume the role. S7's reused policy is an EC2-service-principal instance role (iam.tf:16-28: identifiers = ['ec2.amazonaws.com']), which does not transfer to a web-identity trust relationship. An OIDC role whose trust condition omits a scoped `sub`/`aud` claim (e.g. `repo:<org>/<repo>:ref:refs/heads/main` and the GitHub `aud`) is assumable by other repositories or branches federating through the same GitHub OIDC provider.
findings.location: Approach — 'OIDC federation — permissions: id-token: write plus aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials assuming a dedicated, scoped Bedrock role modelled on S7's POLICY'; AC5 (Bedrock credential mechanism)
scenarios: The OIDC role's trust policy trusts token.actions.githubusercontent.com without a repo/ref sub-claim condition; a fork or another workflow in the org assumes the role and invokes Bedrock on the account's bill
An implementer copies S7's permission policy and, finding no trust-policy guidance, writes an over-broad assume-role condition
findings.suggested_fix: In the Approach and AC5, state the trust-policy subject condition explicitly, e.g. StringEquals aud = sts.amazonaws.com and StringLike sub = repo:<org>/<repo>:ref:refs/heads/main (or the specific workflow/environment). Note that 'modelled on S7's POLICY' covers only the permission grant, since S7's role is EC2-assumed and carries no web-identity trust condition to reuse.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how the per-provider cadence/subset decision (AC7) preserves AC4's guarantee: define a non-empty minimum live-call floor per credentialed provider per trigger it runs on, and extend the fail-on-all-skip canary so a credentialed arm that executed zero live cases fails loudly rather than reading green.
evidence: Plan: 'Decide and record whether every provider runs on every trigger, or whether non-default providers run on a reduced cadence or a reduced case subset.'
AC4: 'An arm whose credential is ABSENT skips LOUDLY ... a missing secret must never read as green.'

tests/external/conftest.py:26-37,84-105 — the tier's own fail-on-all-skip canary is keyed on collected-vs-executed per marker; a reduced-subset arm that executes nothing collides with that oracle's meaning

The plan already treats 'ran and passed' vs 'skipped' as the load-bearing distinction, but a per-provider subset introduces a third state (credentialed-but-ran-nothing-this-trigger) it does not disambiguate
findings.finding: The plan offers a 'reduced case SUBSET per provider' as a live-cadence option but does not reason about how that interacts with the loud-skip / not-green-on-absence requirement: a provider arm that is credentialed but deliberately runs zero (or a trivially small) case subset on a given trigger becomes indistinguishable from a provider arm that silently all-skipped — the exact green-no-op failure the external tier's session-scoped canary (tests/external/conftest.py: _jira_canary_should_fail, fires when collected>=1 and executed==0) exists to prevent.
findings.location: Approach — 'Cost is the real constraint...' paragraph; AC7 (cadence/subset decision) vs AC4 (skip loudly, never read as green)
scenarios: A cost-reduced trigger runs the Bedrock arm with an empty/near-empty case subset; the run is green and reads as 'Bedrock covered' when in fact no live Bedrock call was exercised on that trigger
A future credential outage on a reduced-cadence provider surfaces identically to an intentional zero-case trigger, defeating the loud-skip guarantee

findings.finding: The Bedrock arm's CI credential path and region resolution are asserted but not established for a GitHub-hosted runner. The plan says to 'reuse the S7 access precedent,' but S7 (rebar:9249) grants an EC2 INSTANCE ROLE reachable via IMDS from the review-bot container — a path a `ubuntu-latest` GitHub-hosted runner (external-integration.yml:32) cannot use. The plan names no mechanism (OIDC role assumption vs. static keys in a secret) by which the runner enters the AWS credential chain. Separately, bug rebar:a574 (closed) established that IMDS does NOT supply an AWS region and that Bedrock hard-fails with NoRegionError unless a region is set explicitly; the plan's config file sets only `[llm.model_classes]` and names no region for the CI Bedrock arm.
findings.location: Approach paragraph 4 ('Bedrock authenticates from the AWS credential chain … reuse that precedent'); AC line 'The Bedrock arm authenticates via the AWS credential chain (not an API key), reusing the S7 access precedent'
findings.suggested_fix: In the Approach, replace 'reuse the S7 precedent' for the CI runner with a concrete GitHub-runner credential path — e.g. configure OIDC (`permissions: id-token: write` + aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials) to assume a scoped Bedrock role modeled on S7's policy — and set both AWS_DEFAULT_REGION and REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION as job env for the Bedrock arm. Add an AC that the Bedrock arm resolves a region and fails loudly (typed LLMConfigError, per rebar:a574) rather than skipping silently when the region is absent.
